definitions.explanation: The choice or judgment of when to do something, or the moment at which something happens.

examples.japanese: タイミングが{悪|わる}かった。
{話|はな}しかけるタイミングがつかめなかった。
examples.english: I couldn't find the right moment to speak to them.

examples.japanese: タイミングよく{電車|でんしゃ}が{来|き}たので{待|ま}たずに{乗|の}れた。
examples.english: A train came at just the right moment, so I got on without waiting.

notes:
USAGE:
タイミング is used very broadly in everyday Japanese. Common patterns include タイミングがいい/わるい (good/bad timing), タイミングを{見|み}る ({計|はか}る) (to look for the right moment), and タイミングよく (with good timing, at just the right moment).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- タイミングがいい: good timing
- タイミングが{悪|わる}い: bad timing
- タイミングを{見計|みはか}らう: to watch for the right timing
- タイミングよく: at just the right moment
- タイミングを{逃|のが}す: to miss the timing
